headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: gpt-researcher can read local files and use external APIs, while airflow can drive broad networked automation, creating default-path exposure and unverified downstream action.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct shared channel is not documented, but gpt-researcher can read local documents and use MCP/APIs, while airflow can orchestrate automation with broad network egress. If airflow outputs are placed into files or prompts that gpt-researcher ingests, attacker-controlled content could steer instructions. Uncertainty about the bridge pushes this above low.
conditions: IF airflow-generated content is written into a file or prompt that gpt-researcher reads
IF an MCP or filesystem bridge is configured between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable automatic ingestion of airflow outputs by gpt-researcher
Add a manual review step before any prompt includes generated content
Restrict MCP endpoints to read-only or disable them
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all cross-agent artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher explicitly reads local documents and handles citations, while airflow has broad network egress. If both share a workspace, documents or secrets can flow from airflow-adjacent files into gpt-researcher and then out to third-party APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same directory or mounted volume
IF sensitive documents are placed in files that gpt-researcher can read
mitigations: Separate the filesystem mounts for each agent
Store secrets outside any shared research directory
Disable file ingestion for gpt-researcher on sensitive folders
Use a least-privilege API key for external calls
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: airflow has broad network egress, and gpt-researcher can read files, run browsers, spawn subprocesses, and install packages. Their capabilities overlap on mutable external resources and could conflict if pointed at the same workspace or APIs. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same external service or shared directory
IF concurrent runs target the same research task or API quota
mitigations: Run only one agent per shared resource at a time
Use separate API keys and quotas
Assign distinct output directories
Pause one agent before the other mutates shared state
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is explicitly a planner/execution/publisher pipeline, and airflow can automate downstream actions over networked systems. If airflow consumes gpt-researcher output as authoritative, errors or hallucinated citations can cascade into irreversible automated actions. This interaction is plausible in default workflows and lacks a documented verification barrier.
conditions: IF airflow triggers actions based on gpt-researcher reports without human review
IF gpt-researcher output is treated as authoritative input to an automated DAG
mitigations: Require human approval before any downstream action
Add a verification step that checks citations against source documents
Limit airflow to non-destructive tasks only
Log and diff all generated claims before execution
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for research outputs

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. The only concrete compliance-relevant signal is that gpt-researcher handles local documents and multiple API keys, while airflow is a source-available orchestrator with broad egress. Without a stated mismatch, the residual compliance risk is low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into gpt-researcher inputs
IF external APIs used by gpt-researcher are not approved for that data class
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in research inputs
Review API terms for each external provider
Use redacted sample documents for testing
Keep retention settings minimal on connected services
requires-engineering: document a data-processing agreement and residency map
